messages:
Alex Li: FYI — us-west-2 GPU pool queue spiked around 10:12. p99 gen latency jumped 220ms -> 980ms and queue_len >400 for ~8m. Backpressure began spilling to eu-west and us-east.

Ops-Bot: ALERT: region=us-west-2 gpu_util=94% p99_latency=980ms queue_len=412 spillover -> eu-west:34rps, us-east:15rps

Maria Gomez: Is this a single-tenant burst or many tenants? Any big batches? :thinking:

Alex Li: Not single-tenant. Saw a surge of medium-sized batch reranks + long contexts from a PLG customer.

Samir Patel: Two asks: (1) current admission-control thresholds? (2) do we have per-tenant weights for spill routing in prod?

Devin K: admission-control: global_max_inflight=1200, per_region_share={us-west-2:0.4, eu-west:0.3, us-east:0.3}. No per-tenant weighted spill in prod — only in Canary.

Maria Gomez: Let's avoid blind cross-region spill to eu-west if possible (cost + egress latency). Recommend preferring local fallback model variants and rate-limiting cross-region.

Alex Li: Quick mitigation proposal:
1) drop global_max_inflight -> 960 (20% shed)
2) enable model-fallback mapping for non-SLA tenants: primary rw-instruct-13b-q4 -> fallback rw-instruct-3b-q4 (quantized)
3) set queue_ttl=2s, drop low-priority on expiry
4) enable per-tenant token-buckets to preserve high-value tenants

Samir Patel: +1. Also cap spillover per target region (max_spill_to_region=50rps) and prefer local fallback before cross-region routing.

Devin K: I'll push routing patch to Canary 2, then promote if metrics look good. Patch below.

Devin K: ```
# routing circuit-breaker (canary)
circuit_breaker:
  enable: true
  global_max_inflight: 960
  queue_ttl_ms: 2000
  spillover:
    prefer_local_fallback: true
    max_spill_to_region: 50
    per_tenant_priority: true
fallback_map:
  rw-instruct-13b-q4: rw-instruct-3b-q4
  rw-instruct-65b-q4: rw-instruct-13b-q4
token_bucket:
  capacity_by_tier:
    enterprise: 500
    standard: 200
    free: 50
```

Maria Gomez: Set spill_weight for free tier to 0.2 so they don't get auto-offloaded across zones.

Alex Li: Cost note: full cross-region spill at 500rps ~ +$2.1k/day egress + 30-80ms added p99. Local fallback (quantized) ~ -15% token cost, p99 +20-40ms. Local fallback preferred.

Oncall-Rota: Pagerduty will be paged if p99 > 1s for >5m. We're at 980ms now — monitor closely.

Samir Patel: Add short-term synthetic probes hitting fallback models to check QoE. If quality drift >5% vs baseline, auto-rollback fallback.

Devin K: Rolling Canary in 2m. I'll watch queue_len, spillover_rate, p99_latency, fallback_error_rate.

Maria Gomez: Post-deploy checklist:
- confirm no >15% success-rate drop on 13b->3b fallback for prioritized endpoints
- confirm spill to eu-west capped at 50rps
- record cost delta in #finance for the day

Alex Li: If stable, RFC item: per-tenant spill weights and SLO-based routing (latency SLOs > cost). I'll draft.

Ops-Bot: DEPLOY START: routing-canary/v2 by Devin K

Devin K: Canary looks promising — queue_len down ~40% in 3m, p99 -> 420ms, spillover to eu-west -> 12rps.

Samir Patel: Keep canary for 15m then promote if stable. Any fallback errors?

Devin K: fallback_error_rate ~0.3% (within normal). No QoE alerts triggered.

Alex Li: Action owners: Devin -> promote if stable; Maria -> validate QoE on key customer prompts; Samir -> draft prioritization rules; Alex -> RFC for per-tenant spill strategy. I'll update #incidents if status changes. :thumbsup:

Ops-Bot: DEPLOY SUCCESS: routing-canary/v2 promoted to prod by Devin K

Devin K: Post-promote: queue_len steady ~80, p99 ~260ms, spillover eu-west ~10rps. Cost delta small vs risk reduction.

Maria Gomez: Marking resolved for now. Reopen if p99 >800ms again.

Alex Li: Closing thread — will capture metrics and RFC notes. Great work. :raised_hands:
